units.translation: 21. αἶψα δ’ ἑὸν ἑτά〈ρων〉: ἑὸν is aspirated. For if the initial letters are aspirated and if ever they are transformed, they again have the rough breathing at the beginning, as in ἔρσα, ἑέρση, ἕδνα, ἕεδνα.
22-23a. ἴσχεο νῦν: restrain yourself, whoever you are; for we will obey the laws you speak of. And by not even knowing his name he reproached his inhospitality greatly. L
15b. The phrase ὅτις εὔχεαι is said in contempt. P
25a. 〈ἀπηλεγέως:〉 again instead of 'carelessly'. Lg
b. ἐλίξας: as if turning his eyes upon him. Lg (P)
27. ἰλλόμενος: being rolled up and twisted together. Lg P
28a. ἐπὶ δ’ ὄσσεται οἰόϑεν οἷος: they say that a lion, when wounded, watches only the one who wounded him. So being alone, he looks only at the one who wounded him.
b. οἰόϑεν: alone. And Aristotle (Hist. an. IX 44, 629 b 24) says that the lion does this. L
30. ἐύστιπτον: well-twisted, well-compressed, from στείβειν; whence also στιβάς and στιβεῖς, the fullers.

32-34a. λώπην: a cloak. The sense: he threw off the black double cloak together with its brooches. λώπην means the leather garment. καλαύροπα is a shepherd's staff. And this is because of the man's harshness and wildness.
b. τὴν φορέεσκεν: which he carried, being of wild olive, that is, of the wild olive tree. ὀριτρεφέος means 'of the wild olive nurtured in the mountain'.
35a. ἑαδότα he says meaning the place that pleased. P
10b. 〈ἑαδότα:〉 pleasing. Sm
36. 〈ἕζον:〉 they made to sit down. Sm

38-39a. ὀλοοῖο Τυφωέος: he says this because of the monstrous and extraordinary nature of his body; he was believed, he says, to be the son of Typhon or of Earth, meaning 'great'. It is from the nominative Τυφωεύς.
15b. πέλωρ is said of a beast and something of enormous size. P
40. χωομένη Διί: since Earth is said in anger, when Zeus cast the Titans into Tartarus, to have given birth to the Giants.
42. ἑσπερίην διὰ νύκτα: instead of 'during the night', that is, around evening. Homer (X 318): 'Hesperus, who is fairest in the sky'. ἀμαρυγαί are the rays, the gleams.

43. ἔτι χνοάοντας ἰούλους: having the downy beards, the first growths of the cheeks, still sprouting like down. ἴουλος is also called a many-footed creature and a kind of song, as Eratosthenes says (fg XII Hiller = 241 fg 36 J.).
25 44. Here ἀντέλλειν actively means 'to produce'. P
45-47a. πῆλε δὲ χεῖρας: as if he was making trial of his own hands, whether they were as nimble as before and not sluggish from the toil of rowing. L
b. πῆλε means 'he moved', and πειράζειν means 'to test'. P
48. οὐ μὰν αὖτ’ Ἄμυκ〈ος〉: Amycus did not test himself. And by this he shows his arrogance.
48. οὐ μὰν αὖτ’ Ἄμυκ〈ος〉: Amycus did not test himself. And by this he shows his arrogance.
